definitions.explanation: Describes how something appears on the surface, often implying that the reality underneath may differ. Used to set up a contrast between appearance and actual nature.

examples.japanese: {一見|いっけん}⟦{簡単|かんたん}→簡単：00713_kantan⟧そう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{見|み}える→見える：01165_mieru⟧。
examples.english: It looks simple at first glance.

examples.japanese: {一見|いっけん}⟦{静|しず}か→静か：00755_shizuka⟧だ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{実|じつ}→実：28344_jitsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{活気|かっき}→活気：02554_kakki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦{町|まち}→町：00613_machi⟧だ。
examples.english: It seems quiet at first glance, but it's actually a lively town.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{問題|もんだい}→問題：00797_mondai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{一見|いっけん}{難|むずか}しそうだ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦コツ→コツ：06658_kotsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧つかめば⟦すぐ→すぐ：00814_sugu⟧⟦{解|と}ける→解ける：04371_tokeru⟧。
examples.english: This problem looks difficult at first glance, but once you get the hang of it, you can solve it right away.

notes:
{一見|いっけん} is used to describe surface-level impressions, typically followed by a contrasting reality introduced by が, ⟦けれど→けれど：01990_keredo⟧, or ⟦{実|じつ}→実：28344_jitsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {一見|いっけん}〜そう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{見|み}える→見える：01165_mieru⟧ (looks ~ at first glance)
- {一見|いっけん}〜だ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{実|じつ}→実：28344_jitsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧… (appears ~, but actually…)
- {一見|いっけん}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧ (at a glance, looking at it briefly)
- {一見|いっけん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{価値|かち}→価値：00131_kachi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧ (worth seeing, worth a look)

USAGE:
- Often implies a gap between appearance and reality
- Can be used as a noun meaning "a brief look": {一見|いっけん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{価値|かち}→価値：00131_kachi⟧あり (worth seeing)
- Not to be confused with ⟦{一件|いっけん}→一件：08927_ikken⟧ (one matter/case), which is a homophone
